{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-nj-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"83182b46e6fe160e0801a44aa09dc0469af2cc2c0b1def76511cf17f89bd9f11","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-nj-class-d:lineage:55","source_registry_sha256":"057b72c7c679c997f56ae00ef97a6b14dbe264551f4121b9bf67b0457d9cf7c1","source_liveness_sha256":"1ca7bfbb9e3c0a6b19e5e808ecab6fe8329f3b4799e394abc260d65c1d6513e7"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Sharing the road confusables and continuation details","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: Safe Passing penalties with versus without injury, moped versus low-speed vehicle speeds, right versus left turns near cyclists, and continuation details on pedestrians, motorcycles, scooters, trains, off-road vehicles, animals and horses","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: Safe Passing penalties with versus without injury, moped versus low-speed vehicle speeds, right versus left turns near cyclists, and continuation details on pedestrians, motorcycles, scooters, trains, off-road vehicles, animals and horses
Confusable pairs among sharing-the-road rules, followed by continuation facts the C block left out for size; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec13-R01 | anchor: A08
When turning right, wait for cyclists and skaters to clear and avoid cutting in front of them, but when turning left, yield to oncoming cyclists and skaters and let one ahead of you in the turn lane finish first. [A08]
Why it matters: group cyclists; confusable right turn versus left turn.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0153]

FACT_ID: sec13-R02 | anchor: A07
The bus yield rule covers a bus re-entering traffic from a stop, but once the bus is back in the normal flow, drivers do not have to yield when it changes lanes. [A07]
Why it matters: group buses; confusable re-entering versus changing lanes.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0152]

FACT_ID: sec13-R03 | anchor: A07
Due caution under the Safe Passing Law means slowing down and giving plenty of space, while still obeying every no passing and speed law and moving over a lane when one is available. [A07]
Why it matters: group Safe Passing; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0152]

FACT_ID: sec13-R04 | anchor: A12
Drivers must slow to 25 mph or less near a horse, and must stop completely and wait if a rider coming the other way raises a hand or signals. [A12]
Why it matters: group horses; confusable slowing versus stopping.
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0157]

FACT_ID: sec13-R05 | anchor: A10
A low-speed vehicle has four wheels and can reach more than 20 mph but no more than 25 mph on pavement, and it cannot run on gas or diesel. [A10]
Why it matters: group small vehicles; confusable low-speed vehicle versus moped.
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0155]

FACT_ID: sec13-R06 | anchor: A02
Many pedestrian crashes happen during turns because drivers watch only for other vehicles, so watch for pedestrians when entering or leaving driveways, parking lots and alleys. [A02]
Why it matters: group pedestrians; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0147]

FACT_ID: sec13-R07 | anchor: A03
Pedestrians are harder to see at night and in poor weather, so drivers must slow down and stay more alert after dark. [A03]
Why it matters: group pedestrians; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0148]

FACT_ID: sec13-R08 | anchor: A03
Pedestrians walking where there are no sidewalks should face traffic and wear reflective or light-colored clothing at night, but that never relieves drivers of their duty to stay vigilant. [A03]
Why it matters: group pedestrians; misconception pedestrians carry the burden.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0148]

FACT_ID: sec13-R09 | anchor: A03
Slippery, sloped or uneven pavement and grooves or gratings are hazards for motorcycle riders, so anticipate a rider swerving around something a car would ignore. [A03]
Why it matters: group motorcycles; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0148]

FACT_ID: sec13-R10 | anchor: A03
Watch for motorcycles at intersections and when turning left, always signal, and leave plenty of room between your car and a motorcycle. [A03]
Why it matters: group motorcycles; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0148]

FACT_ID: sec13-R11 | anchor: A08
Before turning, parallel parking, opening a door or pulling from the curb, check blind spots by turning your head rather than relying on mirrors alone. [A08]
Why it matters: group cyclists; difficulty low.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0153]

FACT_ID: sec13-R12 | anchor: A08
A cyclist or skater turning left may use the traffic lanes like a vehicle and may ride along the right edge of the turn lane. [A08]
Why it matters: group cyclists; difficulty medium.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0153]

FACT_ID: sec13-R13 | anchor: A09
Pocket bikes, mini choppers, mini motorcycles and motorized skateboards count as motorized scooters, but e-bikes, low-speed vehicles, motorized wheelchairs and mobility scooters for people with disabilities do not. [A09]
Why it matters: group scooters; confusable what is and is not a motorized scooter.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0154]

FACT_ID: sec13-R14 | anchor: A09
A person with a mobility-related disability may use certain motorized scooters on streets posted at 25 mph or less, and on streets posted up to 35 mph if the local government approves, with a top scooter speed of 15 mph. [A09]
Why it matters: group scooters; difficulty high.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0154]

FACT_ID: sec13-R15 | anchor: A10
A yellow round railroad advance warning sign and white railroad pavement markings tell you a crossing is ahead. [A10]
Why it matters: group trains; difficulty low.
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0155]

FACT_ID: sec13-R16 | anchor: A10
Trains can run on any track, in either direction, at any time, and they are closer and faster than they appear, so never race one to a crossing. [A10]
Why it matters: group trains; misconception the train is far away.
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0155]

FACT_ID: sec13-R17 | anchor: A10
Crossing tracks anywhere except a designated crossing is dangerous and illegal because railroad property is private. [A10]
Why it matters: group trains; difficulty medium.
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0155]

FACT_ID: sec13-R18 | anchor: A11
Snowmobiles, ATVs and dirt bikes may not ride on public roads with other traffic, but they may cross certain roads when it is safe, and their operators must carry proof of insurance and display registration. [A11]
Why it matters: group off-road vehicles; difficulty medium.
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0156]

FACT_ID: sec13-R19 | anchor: A12
Swerving to dodge an animal often causes a crash with something else or a rear-end hit, so watch both sides of the road ahead and be ready for sudden movement. [A12]
Why it matters: group animals; misconception always swerve.
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0157]

FACT_ID: sec13-R20 | anchor: A12
A horse-drawn vehicle must show a front light from 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, whenever visibility is 500 feet or less, and in fog, mist or smoke. [A12]
Why it matters: group horses; difficulty high.
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0157]
